answer: Each agent is one vertex whose work must cross a bridge to count. The vertex locks 80 credits and pays a 20-credit fee, so identity costs 100 credits and the bridge issues a receipt bound to that vertex key. At zenith the bridge publishes crossed work, and auditors sum vertex claims against it. A claim above the total, or a receipt under a second key, is rejected and the bond is burned. The k-th fake identity pays 100 credits, so 1,000 fakes cost 100,000 with no discount, while one honest agent pays 100. A rented bridge receipt names one vertex key; reuse burns both bonds.
